headline: Discussed Veterans Day Parade planning, Veterans Memorial Parkway upkeep, a 9/11 ceremony, and veterans parking ideas; no votes were recorded.
summary: Members discussed planning for the Veterans Day Parade, which will begin in September. They also discussed weeds and graffiti on the Veterans Memorial Parkway and planning for a 9/11 ceremony at the East Hollis Street fire station. The minutes record no votes or formal decisions.
plain_text:
Members Present: Don Vincent, American Legion Post 3; John York, American Legion Post 3; Clayton Proffer, VFW Post 
43; Chairman Lewis Chipola, VFW Post 43; Doug Cotrau, Disabled American Veterans 
Also Present: Emily Vassar-Rivas, Mayor’s Office 
Absent: Steve Ordway (VFW); Marc Plante (VFW); Mayor Jim Donchess 
 
The meeting was called to order at 1505/3:05 PM. 
 
The first item on the agenda was this year’s Veterans Day Parade; L. Chipola asked if there were any updates to share 
from the Parade Committee. John York advised that the planning will begin in September, and Disabled American 
Veterans (DAV) is leading the planning this year. L. Chipola asked if the Army band was planning to participate. J. York 
advised that they are not participating. 
 
The next agenda item was the Veterans Memorial Parkway. L. Chipola advised that overgrown weeds and brush are 
again present along the guardrails and sidewalks, and some poles have graffiti. E. Vassar-Rivas will be reaching out to the 
DPW so that they can send a work crew to address it. Additionally, some banner poles had been bent, presumably by 
high winds, but they were fixed right away. 
 
The next item for discussion was the 9/11 ceremony to be held at the East Hollis Street fire station’s 9/11 Memorial. It is 
coordinated with the Fire Department. J. York will be reaching out at the end of July to find out who in the FD is the 
coordinator, and planning will begin from there. This marks 25 years since the event. 
 
L. Chipola reminded members about the Veterans Coffee Talk Hour held on the second Tuesday of every month at the 
June Caron Senior Center, and encouraged them to spread the word. It is a great way for veterans to network, learn 
about services and programs that benefit them, and socialize. 
 
Post Updates: 
 
• American Legion: J. York announced that the Legion is a recent recipient of charitable gaming funds from the 
Nash Casino. They will be presented with their check at the end of the month. Their committee is hoping to put 
some of the money towards building renovations, such as new lighting. Additionally, they would like to invest in 
a new banner to represent the Post at Holman Stadium. E. Vassar-Rivas asked for an update on the parking 
situation there on Court Street. J. York said it was still not good simply because parking is very limited 
Downtown. Although the Legion has two parking spots in front of the building designated for veterans, many 
Legion members, often with mobility issues, are forced to park quite a way from the Legion. J. York mentioned 
that there are some towns in NH, like Portsmouth, that he’s seen have veteran-focused parking programs that 
allow those with NH veteran plates to park for free throughout the city. E. Vassar-Rivas said she’d look into 
those programs and their structure to see if something similar might be feasible for Nashua. She advised that 
the main hurdle would likely be supplementary funding. 
 
• DAV: D. Cotrau circled back to veterans' parking privileges, specifically those for disabled veterans. A DAV plate 
is akin to a handicap plate, and, like drivers with a handicap plate, DAV drivers can park for free in all municipal 
spaces. 
Mayor’s Veterans Council Meeting                                                                               Monday, July 13, 2026; 1500/3:00 PM
   
City Hall, Room 208
• VFW: L. Chipola mentioned that the VFW is being gifted with a suite at Holman this month for a Silver Knights 
game, which they are looking forward to. On August 16, they will be facilitating a flag-raising ceremony at the 
Nashua Country Club to commemorate the Folds of Honor Golf Tournament. The VFW has been participating 
since 2005, along with a 21-gun detail and a bugler to play Taps to honor servicemen who perished while on 
active duty. The VFW will have a booth at this year’s Gate City Brew Fest on August 22, held at Holman Stadium. 
They plan to have four members present to take shifts manning the booth while others can mingle and enjoy the 
festivities. The event runs from 1:00 PM/1300 to 5:00 PM/1700. This year’s Poppy Drive, organized and run by 
the VFW, will take place as usual this November to coincide with Veterans Day. The drive raises money for a 
relief fund they maintain to help veterans in need with expenses that would otherwise negatively affect their 
lives, such as car repairs and home improvements. C. Proffer expressed his gratitude to the City and Mayor 
Donchess for helping to facilitate the ceremonial raising of the Betsy Ross flag at City Hall Plaza to commemorate 
the 4th of July. It also included the Jr. ROTC, the flag detail, Honor Guard, and the presentation of the Jr. ROTC of 
the Year Award.  
 
 
The meeting was adjourned at 3:35 PM/1535. 
 
The next meeting of the Mayor’s Veterans Council will be held on Monday, September 14, at 3:00 PM/1500 in Room 
208.
